messages:
maria: FYI—EU-west had a short burst at 02:12 UTC; warm-pool didn't replenish fast enough, queue spiked to ~18k and we saw ~1200 429s over ~90s :fire:
autoscaler-bot: AutoScale event: scale_up attempted -> failed to provision 4 nodes in eu-west-1a due to capacity. Provision error: `NO_AVAILABLE_GPU` (ticket #12345)
raj: Looking at admission controller. Token-bucket refill looks fine but warm pool was exhausted. Current live config: `warm_pool.min=6; warm_pool.max=40; warm_pool.replenish_window=90s`
kyle: We can widen `replenish_window` but that delays prewarm reaction. Alternative: short burst prealloc (ephemeral) that can spike to 2x for 2m, then drain. Will cost more for spikes but avoids 429s.
anya: Cost note: 2x prealloc in eu-west increases infra spend ~ $7.2k/mo. But customer SLA hits and Pager fatigue > that during frequent bursts. Could do timeboxed policy (business hours) to reduce $$
maria: Proposal: 1) bump `warm_pool.min` to 12 for eu-west 2) add a "burst prewarm" policy triggered by rising queue slope 3) implement admission soft-shed for non-critical routes when queue>5k 4) run 72h canary in eu-west-1 at 10% traffic
raj: We also need tighter admission thresholds. Current ADM thresholds: `queue_thresholds = { route_critical: 10k, route_default: 5k }`. Suggest route_default -> 3k, add per-tenant burst caps and slow-start backoff for new connections.
kyle: Also lower batching windows for routes that hit queue growth to avoid batch blowups. Suggest `batch.max_delay_ms=15` for hot routes, 40ms for others. That reduces token-per-request churn.
autoscaler-bot: Canary plan prepared: apply to staging, then schedule canary in prod at 03:00 UTC. Rollback triggers: >0.5% 429s over baseline or >20% p95 latency increase.
maria: sgtm. @anya can you greenlight a 2-week budget increase for heated warmpool? @kyle add metric alert for queue slope >2000/min with a paging runbook
anya: Greenlit for 2 weeks but cap budget to $15k. If projection exceeds, we send an exec summary.
raj: I'll run a synthetic spike sim: `tools/spike-sim --shape=double-exponential --peak=6000/s --duration=180s` and attach results here. Expect to test both current config and proposed prewarm policy.
kyle: If sim passes, plan to ship config change to canary (10% traffic) then monitor for 1h before wider rollout. I'll also add a temporary metric `warmpool.replenish_latency`
maria: Thanks. I'll draft a short RFC with timeline and rollback plan. Next actions: raj -> sim + graphs, kyle -> config patch + alert, anya -> budget, autoscaler-bot -> schedule canary.
raj: quick paste of the queue MA over the spike (from monitoring):
```
02:11:50 queue_total=320
02:12:00 queue_total=1200
02:12:20 queue_total=7200
02:12:40 queue_total=12800
02:12:50 queue_total=18000
02:13:30 queue_total=5400
02:14:00 queue_total=800
```
kyle: That slope between 02:12:00->02:12:50 is brutal (~350/s increase average). Burst detection should trigger prewarm at ~1000/min slope, so tweak threshold accordingly.
maria: All right — let's keep the changes small and reversible. We'll reconvene after the sim outputs. :thumbsup:
